messages:
maria p: quick question — as we finalize the audit event v3 shape: what are the minimal fields customers need to be able to validate events themselves, and how does that interact with immutable storage (WORM) + KMS customer-managed keys?

tom h: must-have for customer validation: event_id, schema_version, timestamp, org_id, actor.id, action, resource.id, outcome, signature, signature_key_id. also envelope metadata: encrypted_dek, kms_key_id. for WORM we can only append; schema upgrades need to be additive.

sarah: agreed. add `schema_version` top-level. when introducing required fields later: write default placeholders on ingestion, and include a migration flag in the manifest. customers must be able to verify previous events even after we add fields.

kevin: rotation concern: if customers manage CMKs we should never re-encrypt existing object payloads in place. instead keep original encrypted_DEK with metadata and store rotation chain. suggestion: store `encrypted_dek_chain: [ {kms_key_id, encrypted_dek, rotated_at} ]`. verification should use the encrypted_dek corresponding to the signing key in `signature_key_id`.

julie: example minimal event we discussed:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "3.0",
  "event_id": "evt_01F...",
  "timestamp": "2024-07-09T14:12:03Z",
  "org_id": "org_123",
  "actor": { "id": "user_45", "type": "user", "roles": ["admin"] },
  "action": "iam.role.update",
  "resource": { "type": "role", "id": "role_77" },
  "outcome": "success",
  "signature": "BASE64(...)",
  "signature_key_id": "cust-key-1",
  "encrypted_dek": "BASE64(...)",
  "kms_key_id": "arn:aws:kms:...:key/...",
  "write_digest": "sha256:...",
  "immutability": { "enabled": true, "until": "2031-07-09T14:12:03Z" }
}
```

maria p: that looks good. for customer-facing validation we should publish a small verifier tool (python/ts) that checks signature, digest, and immutability metadata.

tom h: retention/immutability design note: use S3 Object Lock (compliance mode) for WORM, backed by a per-customer CMK. also publish a signed manifest periodically (daily) with root hash of all events for an org and sign it with our attest key so customers can ask for proof-of-retention. store manifests in a separate archive bucket with long retention.

sarah: RBAC change logging: every role change must include `before_roles`, `after_roles`, `changed_by`, `change_ticket`, and a `reason` string. redact PII in resource fields but keep resource identifiers stable.

kevin: vuln triage / incident note: if audit write fails (KMS unavailable, S3 put error), fall back to local durable queue with immediate pager if queue depth > 1000 or write failure persists > 1 minute. incident playbook should include ability to export local queue and ingest to archival store once service restored.

audit-bot: RFC: audit-v3 schema & immutability workflow posted — https://wiki.internal/reports/audit-v3 (please comment)

devops-bot: deploy: branch `audit-v3-schema` deployed to staging — smoke tests passing :rocket:

maria p: action items I will take: 1) open schema PR with the example above + migration notes, 2) draft KMS rotation + encrypted_dek_chain pattern for review, 3) create S3 object lock / manifest template and compliance checklist. will file tickets shortly.

tom h: +1 on the plan. can someone volunteer to own the verifier libs?

sarah: i'll take the python verifier, tom can you do ts?

maria p: perfect — I'll add owners to the tickets and tag security, eng-storage, and devex. thanks all.
